title: ドラえもんのうた (Doraemon no Uta — Doraemon's Song)
description:
The opening theme of the 1979 TV Asahi Doraemon anime, one of the most iconic anime songs in Japanese history. Lyrics by 楠部工 (Kusube Takumi), music by 菊池俊輔 (Kikuchi Shunsuke), performed by 大杉久美子 (Osugi Kumiko) with dialogue by 大山のぶ代 (Oyama Nobuo), the voice of Doraemon for 26 years. The song ran as the opening theme from 1979 to 2005 — an extraordinary 26-year run.

The lyrics express the joys and frustrations of childhood through the lens of Doraemon's magical gadgets: wishing you could fly freely through the sky, lamenting homework and chores, wanting to travel the world. Each verse ends with Doraemon pulling a gadget from his 4D pocket as the answer. The song is as familiar to Japanese people as a nursery rhyme, taught in schools and sung by multiple generations.

For learners: Perfect N5 material. The vocabulary is entirely everyday, child-friendly Japanese. Key words: こんなこと (things like this), できたら (if only I could), いいな (that would be nice / I wish), ゆめ (dream), かなえる (to grant, to make come true), ふしぎ (mysterious, magical), ポッケ (pocket — childlike contraction of ポケット), じゆうに (freely), とびたい (want to fly), だいすき (love / really like). The repeated 'アンアンアン とってもだいすきドラえもん' is one of the most recognised endings in anime.
